emma: Quick heads-up — we saw recurring perf spikes on Mixtral-8x when RoPE mode=NTK and sequence_len > 32k. p95 jumps ~3x on a tiny fraction of requests (long-tail).

perf-bot: ALERT automated: spike detected on mixtral-8x-prod: avg_p95=340ms -> 1020ms (window 03:14-03:22). KV-cells increased by 2.1x during spikes.

dmitri: Is this the same pattern as the yarn/linear regressions from last month? or a new mode-specific hysteresis?

emma: Different: earlier was steady drift with batching. This is sudden when requests include deep-rewind prompts (lots of short prefixes + one huge appended doc). KV cache growth + kernel fallback observed.

sophie: Can you paste the profiler snapshot?

emma: Pasting condensed flame and timings:
```
# profiler summary (03:16)
model: mixtral-8x
rope: NTK, alpha=0.8
seq_len=34000
requests: 1200
p50=65ms p95=1020ms p99=1800ms
kv_mem_peak=12.3GB (expected 5.6GB)
kernel_path: aten->fallback->cuda_slow_kernel
batching: continuous batching disabled on spike due to evict jitter
```

mike: kv_mem_peak x2.2 is the smoking gun. Why did KV grow that much? Are we duplicating slots or not evicting prefixes?

emma: Two things: NTK RoPE mapping increases effective position indexes for far tokens -> larger internal KV index mapping + our eviction policy was LRU-by-last-access which fails with repeated long rewinds (prefix re-access pattern). Also observed head-kv slice expansion on Mixtral config when heads=64 kv_dim=128, we allocate extra buffer for head-slice alignment.

dmitri: Hmm. So combination: NTK scaling expands pos idx *and* Mixtral's head alignment causes rounding, leading to >2x memory. Kernel selection then falls back because the optimized kernels were tuned for smaller kv footprint.

perf-bot: NOTE: kernel_fallback_count increased by 43% during window.

sophie: Any differences vs Llama and Qwen on same workload?

emma: Quick cross-model numbers (same input trace):
- mixtral-8x (NTK alpha=0.8): p95=1020ms, kv_peak=12.3GB, ppx_delta +0.12 (perplexity slight increase)
- mixtral-8x (linear): p95=180ms, kv_peak=5.9GB, ppx_delta 0.00
- qwen-14b (NTK alpha=0.8): p95=220ms, kv_peak=6.1GB, ppx_delta +0.03
- llama-13b (NTK alpha=0.8): p95=260ms, kv_peak=6.8GB, ppx_delta +0.05

mike: So Mixtral is disproportionately impacted. Likely the head/kv_dim packing is the multiplier. Could be our padding/align logic for head slices.

dmitri: Proposed mitigation ideas:
1) Soft-eviction: prefer evicting long-inactive prefix chains earlier for NTK mode (heuristic: shorten retention when seq_len_growth > threshold).
2) Dynamic RoPE bucketization: map far positions into coarse buckets past a cutoff to reduce unique KV addresses (approximate NTK -> hybrid linear above cutoff).
3) Kernel-aware allocation: avoid oversized head-slice rounding by packing tail-only heads into compact buffers when contiguous.
4) Quick circuit-breaker: if kv_mem > 9GB for Mixtral-8x, immediately switch RoPE -> linear for that request and mark as degraded (log + metric).

sophie: I like 2 + 4 for quick production safety. 1 is medium-risk for quality. 3 requires runtime allocator changes but is high-value.

emma: Ran a short AB: dynamic bucketization (bucket_cutoff=8k, buckets=256) vs circuit-breaker. Results:
- bucketization: p95=240ms, kv_peak=6.2GB, ppx_delta +0.06 (quality hit small, fewer per-token diffs)
- circuit-breaker (fallback->linear): p95=210ms, kv_peak=5.9GB, ppx_delta +0.10 (some outputs degrade on long-coherent documents)

mike: Good. Which one to default? bucketization seems safer quality-wise.

dmitri: We should also update kernel-picker: if estimated_kv_cells > X then route to linear-optimized kernel path proactively to avoid fallback overhead (avoid paying kernel_fallback cost mid-request). Also a scheduling hint to avoid batching with small-fast requests that would raise p95 for others.

perf-bot: TODO created: PERF-312: implement bucketized-NTK hybrid + kernel-picker mem threshold. Assignee: dmitri. SLA target: p95 < 300ms for long-tail sweep.

sophie: Experiment plan:
- Stage A: rollout bucketized NTK on canary Mixtral-8x (5% traffic) for 48h — monitor p95/p99, ppx and kernel_fallbacks.
- Stage B: add proactive kernel-picker threshold to avoid on-the-fly fallback (server-side heuristic only).
- Stage C: evaluate soft-eviction policies (simulate on recorded traces first).

emma: I've got traces and a replay harness. I'll run the Stage A ablation (cutoffs 4k/8k/16k) and push perf traces.

mike: Also add a short-term alert rule: if kernel_fallback_count > baseline*1.3 AND kv_mem_peak > model_specific_threshold raise P1 alert. We had too many passive regressions.

emma: Agreed. Assigning:
- dmitri: implement bucketized mapping + kernel-picker threshold (PR -> review by sophie)
- emma: run replay + ablation, produce perf dashboard
- sophie: vet quality regressions on eval set (long-doc coherence)
- mike: tweak alerts and rollout schedule

perf-bot: Comment: linked traces: s3://redwood-perf/traces/1755555555-mixtral-ntk-spike.tar.gz

dmitri: I'll start a branch today. Expect first bench numbers by EOD PST.

emma: Thanks — will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
